findings.explanation: HLD_GCP_376 only checks that config.web_server_network_access_control is set (not_null); it can't see the value supplied at the call site. This example instantiates the module with web_server_allowed_ip_range = "0.0.0.0/0", so the Airflow web UI - which exposes DAG code, Airflow Connections/Variables (frequently holding credentials), and the ability to trigger DAG runs - is reachable from the entire internet. private_environment_config.enable_private_endpoint = true only privatizes the GKE control-plane endpoint; the web server allowlist is the only network control governing who reaches the UI, and it is set to allow everyone.
findings.remediation: In example/examplea/module.composer.tf, set web_server_allowed_ip_range to a specific, narrow CIDR (e.g. a corporate VPN range) instead of 0.0.0.0/0.
findings.title: Composer web server IP allowlist configured as 0.0.0.0/0, negating HLD_GCP_376's protection

findings.explanation: HLD_GCP_159 only checks that kms_key_name is set on the environment; it has no visibility into whether the key's IAM policy actually grants access. Cloud Composer's CMEK provisioning requires the Cloud Composer Service Agent (service-PROJECT_NUMBER@cloudcomposer-accounts.iam.gserviceaccount.com) to hold roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the key. No google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member or _binding exists anywhere in this repo for google_kms_crypto_key.main, so `terraform apply` will succeed at the plan/resource-creation level but Composer environment provisioning itself will fail with a permission-denied error referencing the key. This exact companion-grant pattern already has dedicated holden policies for Cloud SQL, GCS, Filestore, Healthcare, Document AI, Cloud Run, Workflows, and Pub/Sub (e.g. HLD_GCP_453) - Cloud Composer is a gap in that family.
findings.title: CMEK key has no IAM grant for the Composer service agent - environment provisioning will fail

findings.explanation: variables.tf defines var.name specifically so each Composer environment instantiated by this module has a distinct identity, but iam.tf:2 hardcodes account_id = "composer-env-account" instead of deriving it from var.name. GCP service account IDs must be unique per project, so instantiating this reusable module a second time in the same project (a second environment, or a staging+prod pair) will fail with an 'already exists' error on the second apply. This is only visible by reading variables.tf and iam.tf together - a rule checking iam.tf in isolation sees a syntactically unremarkable service account.
findings.remediation: Derive account_id from var.name (e.g. account_id = "composer-${var.name}"), and add a format-constraining validation block to var.name in variables.tf (lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens, 6-30 chars, starts with a letter) so the derived ID is always a valid GCP service account ID.
findings.title: Composer service account ID is hardcoded, not parameterized by var.name - module can't be safely instantiated twice in one project

suggested_policies.rationale: coverage_by_type["google_composer_environment"] lists only HLD_GCP_100/158/159/374/375/376 - none checks that a companion google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member/_binding grants the Composer service agent access to the CMEK key referenced by encryption_config.kms_key_name. This exact requires_companion pattern is already established for eight other GCP resource types (google_sql_database_instance/HLD_GCP_453, google_storage_bucket, google_filestore_instance, healthcare datasets, Document AI processors, Cloud Run, Workflows, Pub/Sub topics) - Composer is a gap in an otherwise-consistent family, and the pattern fires correctly on any Terraform using google_composer_environment with CMEK, not just this repo. Validated with `holden validate-policy` (OK) and test-scanned against this repo: correctly returns UNKNOWN (not a false PASS) since the module boundary /kms_key_name = var.kms_key_name/ isn't statically resolvable without a --plan file - matches the documented behavior of the sibling CMEK-companion policies.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_001
name: Cloud Composer CMEK key must grant the Composer service agent Encrypter/Decrypter access
principle: encryption
severity: HIGH
rationale: |
  Setting config.encryption_config.kms_key_name on a google_composer_environment
  only tells the environment which key to use — it doesn't grant access to it.
  Cloud Composer's CMEK provisioning requires the Cloud Composer Service Agent
  (service-PROJECT_NUMBER@cloudcomposer-accounts.iam.gserviceaccount.com) to
  hold roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on that key before the
  environment can be created. HLD_GCP_159 already requires kms_key_name to be
  set; this policy requires the companion grant that makes it actually work.
  Without a matching google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member (or _binding) granting
  that role on the same key, environment creation fails at provisioning time
  with a permission-denied error referencing the key, even though the
  Terraform plan itself succeeds and nothing on the
  google_composer_environment resource surfaces the missing prerequisite.
remediation: |
  Grant the Cloud Composer service agent access to the key referenced:

  ```hcl
  data "google_project" "current" {}

  resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member" "composer_cmek" {
    crypto_key_id = google_kms_crypto_key.main.id
    role          = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
    member        = "serviceAccount:service-${data.google_project.current.number}@cloudcomposer-accounts.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_composer_environment:
    filter:
      path: config.encryption_config.kms_key_name
      not_null: true
    requires_companion:
      type: google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member
      linked_via:
        from: config.encryption_config.kms_key_name
        to: crypto_key_id
      where:
        path: role
        equals: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter

suggested_policies.rationale: HLD_GCP_376 (coverage_by_type["google_composer_environment"]) only checks config.web_server_network_access_control is not_null - it never inspects what the allowed_ip_range entries actually permit. A companion policy that fails specifically on a 0.0.0.0/0 entry closes that gap without duplicating HLD_GCP_376, mirrors existing 'don't allow 0.0.0.0/0' checks elsewhere in the catalog (e.g. security-group-style rules), and fires correctly on any Terraform using google_composer_environment, not just this repo. Validated with `holden validate-policy` (OK). Test-scanned against this repo: currently PASSes at the module's own resource declaration because web_server_allowed_ip_range is a var reference at that scope and holden's static resolver doesn't chase it through the module call site without a --plan file - the same documented 'variables / cross-module' blind spot noted for holden-ai-review itself, not a defect in the policy's DSL expression.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_002
name: Cloud Composer web server IP allowlist must not permit unrestricted access
principle: network-security
severity: HIGH
rationale: |
  HLD_GCP_376 requires web_server_network_access_control to be set, but only
  checks that the block exists — it does not check what the allowed_ip_range
  entries actually allow. Configuring allowed_ip_range with value = "0.0.0.0/0"
  satisfies the existence check while granting every IPv4 address on the
  internet access to the Airflow web UI, which exposes DAG code, Airflow
  Connections/Variables (which frequently hold credentials), and the ability
  to trigger DAG runs. The network-access-control feature only provides the
  restriction its name implies when the configured ranges are actually
  narrower than the entire internet.
remediation: |
  Scope allowed_ip_range.value to a specific, narrower CIDR range, not 0.0.0.0/0:

  ```hcl
  resource "google_composer_environment" "main" {
    config {
      web_server_network_access_control {
        allowed_ip_range {
          value       = "203.0.113.0/24"
          description = "corp office range"
        }
      }
    }
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_composer_environment:
    path: config.web_server_network_access_control.allowed_ip_range
    not_any:
      path: value
      cidr_prefix_lte: 0
